name: Pipedream
summary: Pipedream runs workflows made of ready-made app steps and your own code, started by a web address, a schedule or an app event, on Pipedream's servers.

free_plan_covers.note: The Free plan gives up to 100 credits a month, 3 active workflows and 3 connected accounts. A credit is 30 seconds of run time, so most short runs use one credit each: about 100 runs a month.

first_paid_usd_month.note: The Basic plan is $45 a month billed monthly, or $29 a month billed yearly ($348 a year), and includes 2,000 credits a month. The pricing page only shows these numbers after it loads in a browser.

portability.note: Code steps are ordinary Node.js, Python, Go or Bash you can copy out, but triggers, connected accounts and the steps around them are Pipedream's own and need rebuilding elsewhere.

self_hostable.note: Workflows run on servers Pipedream manages. Its library of app steps is published as source code, but the platform that runs workflows isn't offered for your own server.

code_steps.note: Code steps run Node.js 20, Python, Go or Bash inside a workflow. Runs stop after 30 seconds by default for web requests, up to 5 minutes on the free plan and 12.5 minutes on paid plans.

webhook_triggers.note: An HTTP trigger gives the workflow its own web address that accepts any request. It needs no password by default; you can add a token check.

setup.step: Create a free Pipedream account and start a new workflow.
Pick the HTTP / Webhook trigger, add token checking, and copy the workflow's address into your app's environment file.

builder_notes: Call the Pipedream webhook from server code only, reading the address from PIPEDREAM_WEBHOOK_URL; the address works without a password unless the workflow checks a token.
Keep each run short: a web request trigger stops after 30 seconds by default, and longer runs use more credits.
